scope: Regulatory/screening source corrections only; no live screening, comprehensive jurisdiction survey or legal certification.
date_semantics: Null dates mean not established or no single applicable date; publication, effective, compliance and review dates are not interchangeable. READ means page/PDF retrieved; SEARCH_EXCERPT means only indexed primary-source text was inspected. UNAVAILABLE records failed access, not absence of a rule.

sources.date_basis: Statement dated 19 June 2026; not a domestic-law effective date
sources.conclusion: Grey-listing alone is not a FATF call for EDD. Check current statements and domestic measures; no country list is embedded.

sources.conclusion: Former PEP treatment is risk-based, not an automatic fixed-period expiry. Domestic implementation and PEP category matter.

sources.date_basis: 15 USC 80a-2(a)(51); historical effective dates require transaction-specific review
sources.conclusion: QP trust route depends on decision-maker and contributors and formation conditions; not a generic $5m trust-assets test.

sources.date_basis: Agency overview; verify counting rules and offering conditions separately
sources.conclusion: Ordinary 3(c)(1), qualifying VC and 3(c)(7) are separate routes; accredited status is not itself the 3(c)(1) exclusion.

sources.conclusion: Qualifying-VC capital threshold adjusted to $12m; additional conditions and 250-owner route must be tested separately.

sources.conclusion: At least $1.4m managed assets or net worth greater than $2.7m for the monetary routes, subject to scope, other routes and transition rules.

sources.date_basis: Reference paper form SEC 2048 (4-25); online file may include deferred amendments
sources.conclusion: Baseline $150m filing scope; large hedge $1.5bn and large PE $2bn. Sections 2/3/4 differ. Event reporting is not a universal 72-hour PE obligation. Select operative version using the extension below.

sources.conclusion: Defers compliance only for amendments adopted 8 February 2024 to 1 July 2027; not all Form PF rules. Existing obligations continue; 2026 proposed amendments remain proposals.

sources.date_basis: Instructions revision June 2022; claim-specific validity exceptions
sources.conclusion: General W-8 validity ends in the third succeeding calendar year, subject to exceptions and invalidating changes; not a universal third anniversary.

sources.date_basis: Revision October 2021; verify form revision at use
sources.conclusion: Part III treaty; XXV active NFFE; XXVI passive NFFE; XXIX owner disclosure; XXX certification. Other categories require their actual instructions.

sources.date_basis: 2025 consolidated standard; not automatic simultaneous domestic commencement
sources.conclusion: Controlling persons, passive-NFE treatment and reportability require local implementation and current reportable-jurisdiction lists, not nationality alone.

sources.conclusion: Form 990-T covers applicable IRA trusts and exempt organisations; gross unrelated-business-income filing threshold is distinct from final taxable income and tax due.

sources.date_basis: Current agency guidance; verify tax-year law and partner circumstances
sources.conclusion: Section 1446 ECTI withholding differs from FDAP withholding; do not apply a flat 30% FDAP rate to all ECI.

sources.conclusion: Previously embedded 2023-level figures labelled 2025 were stale. Skills now require tax-year-specific instructions rather than a static threshold.

sources.conclusion: Significant participation begins at 25%, with class, exclusion and look-through analysis. Operating-company exceptions are separate tests.

sources.conclusion: Use actual EUR-based AIFMD reporting rules, manager/fund scope and local authority instructions, not the removed US-dollar bands.

sources.conclusion: No assurance of current consolidated SFDR templates; obtain the official version before use.

sources.date_basis: Proposed 20 April 2026; comment period closed 23 June 2026. Details read in law-firm summaries (Morrison Foerster 19 May 2026; Mayer Brown 28 Apr 2026), not the proposing release. Any compliance date would follow adoption.
sources.conclusion: PROPOSED ONLY: would raise the Form PF filing threshold from $150m to $1bn and the large hedge threshold from $1.5bn to $10bn, remove quarterly PE event reporting and set 72 hours for large-hedge current reports. Show as a watch item or labelled scenario; never apply to a current period. IA-6992 (1 July 2027) supersedes the 1 Oct 2026 date some summaries still cite.

sources.date_basis: Staff statement for FY2026 (released Nov 2025); not a rule
sources.conclusion: Core areas named: marketing, valuation, trading, portfolio management, disclosure and filings, custody; annual compliance-programme review; Schedules 13D/G, Form 13F, Forms 3/4/5 and N-PX filings for some advisers; differential treatment of investors including side letters; Regulations S-ID and S-P. Priorities, not legal requirements.

sources.date_basis: Amendments adopted 16 May 2024 (Exchange Act Release 100155). Two compliance dates by entity size: 3 December 2025 (larger entities, advisers with at least $1.5bn AUM) and 3 June 2026 (smaller entities); read in a law-firm summary dated 7 May 2026, not the release itself.
sources.conclusion: Written incident-response programme; notice to affected individuals not later than 30 days after becoming aware of an incident; service providers to notify within 72 hours. Compliance: larger entities (advisers with at least $1.5bn AUM) 3 Dec 2025, smaller entities 3 Jun 2026. Event-driven duties.

sources.date_basis: Private Fund Adviser Rules vacated by the Fifth Circuit effective 5 June 2024; SEC technical amendments (IA-6773) effective 19 November 2024
sources.conclusion: Quarterly statement, private fund audit, restricted activities and preferential treatment rules, and the related 206(4)-7 annual-review documentation amendment, are vacated. Never flag their requirements as missing; side-letter scrutiny now rests on exams and anti-fraud rules.

sources.date_basis: Staff FAQs on Rule 206(4)-1; updates dated 19 March 2025 (extracted performance, portfolio characteristics) and 15 January 2026 (model fees; testimonials from persons with SRO disqualifications)
sources.conclusion: Staff guidance, not rule text. Cite by FAQ date when reviewing marketing material for extracted performance, net performance and model fees.

sources.date_basis: Rule text read on Cornell LII because eCFR redirected to a bot check; canonical source is eCFR. 2023 Safeguarding proposal reported withdrawn 12 June 2025 (search snippet only).
sources.conclusion: Pooled-vehicle audit route: audited financial statements distributed within 120 days of the end of the fiscal year (other periods for funds of funds need separate verification). Qualified custodian requirements remain. Reform timing unknown.

sources.date_basis: Rule text read on Cornell LII; canonical source is eCFR
sources.conclusion: Annual updating amendment to Form ADV within 90 days of the end of the adviser's fiscal year; other-than-annual amendments promptly when specified information becomes inaccurate. Derive the date from the evidenced fiscal year end and label it derived.

sources.date_basis: Rule text read on Cornell LII; canonical source is eCFR
sources.conclusion: Form D due no later than 15 calendar days after the first sale; annual amendment on or before the anniversary while the offering continues; other amendment triggers per the rule. State notice filings are separate.

sources.date_basis: Rule text read on Cornell LII; canonical source is eCFR
sources.conclusion: Large trader: identifying activity level of 2 million shares or $20 million in a day, or 20 million shares or $200 million in a calendar month. Initial Form 13H promptly after first effecting aggregate transactions at that level; annual filing within 45 days after each full calendar year; amended filing promptly after the end of a quarter in which information became inaccurate.

sources.date_basis: Staff FAQ; 45 days after quarter end, rolled to the next business day when the 45th day falls on a weekend or holiday (Q2 2026 example: 14 August 2026)
sources.conclusion: Form 13F scope turns on section 13(f) securities and investment discretion, not total AUM. Deadlines derived from quarter end are labelled derived; business-day rolls are not computed by the packaged helper.

sources.date_basis: Rule text read on Cornell LII; canonical source is eCFR. State and local pay-to-play rules not researched.
sources.conclusion: Two-year time-out after a covered associate's contribution to an official of a government entity; de minimis $350 per official per election where entitled to vote and $150 otherwise; six-month look-back for new covered associates; applies through covered investment pools.

sources.date_basis: Rule text read on Cornell LII shows base amounts; current dollar thresholds are set by order (IA-6961, effective 29 June 2026; see sec-qualified-client)
sources.conclusion: Use the thresholds in force on the contract date, with transition provisions. Base amounts in the rule text are not the current thresholds.

sources.authority: EU (Directive (EU) 2024/927; summary by Norton Rose Fulbright, Regulation Tomorrow)
sources.date_basis: Transposition deadline 16 April 2026, read in a law-firm summary dated 16 April 2026 (also Ocorian, 24 April 2026). Secondary source only: the directive text on EUR-Lex, including Art. 2 application dates for new Annex IV reporting, was not retrieved.
sources.conclusion: Operational rules (liquidity management tools for open-ended AIFs, delegation, loan-origination retention and leverage limits, disclosure of fees and charges) apply under national law from 16 April 2026. New Annex IV reporting templates await ESMA technical standards; do not schedule a new-template filing date.

sources.date_basis: Commission proposal COM(2025) 841 of 20 November 2025; Council position 24 June 2026 and Parliament committee mandate 10 September 2026 seen in secondary sources; application 18 or 24 months after entry into force
sources.conclusion: PROPOSED ONLY: would replace Article 6/8/9 disclosures with three product categories (Transition, ESG Basics, Sustainable) each with a 70% threshold, remove entity-level PAI statements and repeal RTS 2022/1288, with grandfathering for existing closed-ended funds. Current SFDR and RTS 2022/1288 still apply.

sources.date_basis: Guidelines apply 3 months after publication in all EU languages; existing funds had a further 6 months. Application dates are derived, not read.
sources.conclusion: Funds using ESG or sustainability-related terms in their names apply an 80% threshold of investments meeting the promoted characteristics or objectives, plus the specified exclusions. Differs from the 70% threshold in the SFDR 2.0 proposal.

sources.date_basis: PS23/16 timeline: anti-greenwashing rule 31 May 2024; labels 31 July 2024; naming and marketing 2 December 2024; entity-level disclosures for firms over GBP 50bn AUM 2 December 2025 and over GBP 5bn 2 December 2026. FCA page update of 5 June 2026 not read.
sources.conclusion: UK SDR scope depends on the firm and product; anti-greenwashing applies to all FCA-authorised firms. Verify the current timeline before scheduling entity-level disclosures.

sources.conclusion: Voluntary framework, not a legal obligation. Use the reporting-year metric specification; eight core metrics.
